toc.title: Datasets, approaches, metrics, business objectives and practice

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Choose an evaluation approach: human-in-the-loop, benchmark datasets and Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
  • Pick a metric: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation (ROUGE), Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU), BERTScore and LLM-as-a-judge
  • Judge whether a model meets business objectives
  • Evaluate RAG, agents and workflows, and name business alignment metrics

2Datasets, approaches, metrics, business objectives and practice

Running case

Cedar and Salt Tests Before Launch

  • Leaders will launch the assistant only if it is good enough
  • The team has candidate models, a knowledge base and an agent to compare
  • Reviewers disagree on tone, and thousands of answers are too many to read
  • Your job: pick the approach and the metrics that prove it

Why Evaluate, and with What Data

  • Evaluation is the most critical and challenging part of building generative AI, because outputs are unstructured and subjective
  • Use a mix: automated metrics, model-based scoring and human review
  • Start with a golden dataset of question and answer pairs, ideally human-curated
  • Sources: real logs, expert-written examples and synthetic data that you check carefully
  • Ground truth can be a reference text or a list of expected facts
  • Choose metrics that fit the business problem

Exam tip: One metric is never enough: combine automated, model-based and human evaluation.

Benchmark Datasets and Built-In Tasks

Task type Built-in dataset Accuracy measure
Text summarization Gigaword BERTScore
Question and answer BoolQ, NaturalQuestions, TriviaQA F1 score
Text classification Women's E-Commerce Clothing Reviews Classification accuracy
General text generation TREX Real world knowledge score
  • Amazon Bedrock also scores robustness and toxicity
  • Use a built-in benchmark dataset or your own custom prompt dataset

Exam tip: A benchmark dataset gives a fair, repeatable test; a custom dataset tests your use case.

Evaluation Approaches in Amazon Bedrock

  • Programmatic: computed scores on a built-in or custom dataset
  • Human workers: employees or subject-matter experts rate the answers
  • Judge model: a second LLM scores each answer and explains why
  • RAG evaluation: checks a knowledge base for retrieval and answers

Exam tip: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation covers automatic, human, judge-model and RAG evaluations.

ROUGE and BLEU

Metric What it measures Typical use
ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation) N-gram overlap with a reference, focusing on recall Summarization and question answering
BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) N-gram overlap, focusing on precision; penalizes short outputs Machine translation
  • Both are fast, cheap and objective, and both need a reference text
  • Both miss meaning and penalize valid rephrasing

Exam tip: Recall and summaries: ROUGE. Precision and translation: BLEU.

BERTScore

  • BERTScore compares the embeddings of the generated text and the reference text
  • It measures semantic similarity, so a paraphrase can still score well
  • It captures meaning better than word overlap, but costs more compute
  • It also needs a reference text
  • Amazon Bedrock uses BERTScore as the accuracy measure for summarization
  • METEOR is another overlap metric that also credits synonyms and stems

Exam tip: Same meaning, different words: BERTScore.

LLM-as-a-Judge

  • A second LLM, the judge, scores another model's answers and explains each score
  • The job needs a generator model and an evaluator model
  • Built-in metrics: correctness, completeness, faithfulness, helpfulness, coherence, relevance, following instructions, tone, harmfulness, stereotyping and refusal; you can add custom metrics
  • It is faster and cheaper than people, but a judge can be biased
  • Use a judge from a different model family, validate it against people, and keep humans for critical decisions

Exam tip: Scoring thousands of answers with explanations: LLM-as-a-judge.

Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation

  • People are the ultimate source of truth for quality
  • In Amazon Bedrock the work team can be your employees or subject-matter experts
  • They rate answers on a scale or compare two outputs
  • Best for subjective qualities such as tone, style and brand voice
  • Downsides: slow, expensive and sometimes inconsistent
  • Use people to build the golden dataset, audit the judge, and act as the final quality gate

Exam tip: Subjective quality, such as tone: add human evaluation.

Evaluating RAG, Agents and Workflows [Verify live]

  • RAG, retrieve only: does the knowledge base fetch relevant passages?
  • RAG, retrieve and generate: is the final answer correct, complete and faithful to the sources?
  • A RAG evaluation needs a dataset with ground truth: the expected texts and responses
  • Agents: AgentCore Evaluations scores an agent's traces with built-in or custom evaluators, using LLM-as-a-judge
  • Workflows: evaluate each step, not only the final result
  • As of 5 November 2026: AgentCore Evaluations works with frameworks such as Strands and LangGraph

Exam tip: Judge the retrieval step and the answer step separately.

Do the Results Meet Business Objectives?

Business alignment metric What it tells you
Productivity Time or effort saved per task
User engagement How often and how long people use it
Task completion rate Share of tasks the assistant finishes successfully
User satisfaction What users rate their experience
Cost per interaction AI cost per conversation or request
  • Pair model metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore) with business metrics

Exam tip: A good score on ROUGE does not prove business value; task completion and satisfaction do.

What the Exam Asks: Evaluation

  • Which approach: human-in-the-loop, benchmark dataset, Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation or judge model
  • Which metric: ROUGE for summaries, BLEU for translation, BERTScore for meaning, LLM-as-a-judge for scale
  • Which target: a model, a RAG system, an agent or a workflow
  • Which business measure: productivity, engagement, task completion, satisfaction or cost per interaction

Exam tip: Name what you are judging first, then the approach and the metric.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt's Launch Review

What the team needs Name and answer
Compare summaries with reference summaries by word overlap ROUGE
Check a translated policy against a human translation BLEU
Summaries paraphrase the reference but mean the same BERTScore
Score thousands of answers quickly, with reasons LLM-as-a-judge
Judge the warmth of the tone Human evaluation
Check that the knowledge base fetches the right passages RAG evaluation, retrieve only
Show the assistant helps guests book Task completion rate and satisfaction
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

3Exam Q&A

3.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Which metric measures n-gram overlap with a reference text, focuses on recall and is commonly used for summarization?

  • ABLEU
  • BROUGE
  • CBERTScore
  • DWord error rate
Show the answer

Answer: B. ROUGE, Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation, measures n-gram overlap and focuses on recall, so it suits summarization. BLEU focuses on precision and suits translation, and BERTScore compares embeddings.

S2Cedar and Salt's tool writes summaries that paraphrase the reference summaries. Which metric captures the shared meaning better than exact word overlap?

  • AROUGE
  • BBLEU
  • CBERTScore
  • DToxicity score
Show the answer

Answer: C. BERTScore compares the embeddings of the generated and reference text, so it measures semantic similarity and gives credit to paraphrases. ROUGE and BLEU depend on matching words.

S3Which TWO statements about ROUGE and BLEU are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AROUGE focuses on recall and is common for summarization
  • BBLEU focuses on recall and is common for summarization
  • CBLEU focuses on precision and is common for translation
  • DBoth metrics work without any reference text
  • EBoth metrics measure the toxicity of generated text
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. ROUGE is recall-oriented and used for summaries; BLEU is precision-oriented and used for machine translation. Both compare generated text with a reference text, and neither measures toxicity.

S4Cedar and Salt must score thousands of assistant answers quickly, with an explanation for each score. Which approach fits best?

  • AAsk staff members to rate every answer by hand
  • BCompare each answer with a fixed text by exact match
  • CWait for guest complaints, then review those answers
  • DRun a job that uses a judge model to score the answers
Show the answer

Answer: D. A model evaluation job that uses a judge model scores each response and explains the score, and it scales far better than human review. Keep people for subjective or critical decisions.

S5Which statement describes a benefit of human-in-the-loop evaluation of a foundation model?

  • AIt judges subjective qualities such as tone better than fixed metrics
  • BIt is always faster and cheaper than any automatic or model-based metric
  • CIt gives identical scores from every reviewer every single time they rate
  • DIt needs no evaluation criteria, reference text or rating scale to run
Show the answer

Answer: A. People are best at subjective qualities such as tone, style and brand voice, and they calibrate automatic and judge-model scores. Human review is slower, costlier and can vary between reviewers.

S6Leaders ask whether the booking assistant meets the company's business objectives. Which measures fit best?

  • AThe ROUGE score of the review summaries
  • BThe BLEU score of the translated policy pages
  • CTask completion rate and user satisfaction
  • DThe number of parameters in the model
Show the answer

Answer: C. Business alignment metrics include productivity, user engagement, task completion rate, user satisfaction and cost per interaction. ROUGE and BLEU score text quality, and model size does not measure business results.

4Quick Reference Card
